section1.paragraph1: The Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS) observes our ocean through the "eyes" of thousands of ocean observing platforms that are constantly monitoring the ocean to capture the signature of various ocean phenomena.
section1.paragraph2: To highlight the status and development of this Global Ocean Observing System, the 2023 Ocean Observing System Report Card provides insight into the current status of the global observing networks.

quote.text: In the face of climate change, the global community must work together to improve the coverage, quality, and multidisciplinary nature of the observing system to meet vital forecasting services and societal needs. OceanOPS can help make these connections

indicatorsModal.title: Network Performance Indicators
indicatorsModal.intro: Each network is evaluated across five key performance indicators, rated on a scale from 0 to 3 stars:

implementationStatus.title: Implementation Status
implementationStatus.description: Measures the network's operational maturity and geographic coverage. Higher ratings indicate broader global deployment and consistent data collection.

realTime.title: Real Time Data Delivery
realTime.description: Evaluates the timeliness of data transmission to operational centers. Networks with high ratings provide data within hours of collection, supporting immediate forecasting needs.

archivedHighQuality.title: Archived High Quality Data
archivedHighQuality.description: Assesses the completeness and quality control of historical data archives. High ratings indicate rigorous quality assurance processes and comprehensive long-term records.

metadata.title: Metadata Completeness
metadata.description: Measures the documentation of observation methods, instruments, and data provenance. Complete metadata ensures data can be properly interpreted and reused by the scientific community.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices Adoption
bestPractices.description: Evaluates adherence to international standards for data collection, processing, and sharing. Networks following best practices ensure data interoperability across systems.

introduction.paragraph1: The Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS) observes our ocean through the eyes of thousands of ocean observing platforms that are constantly monitoring the ocean to capture the signature of various ocean phenomena.
introduction.paragraph2: These platforms collect physical, biogeochemical and biological Essential Ocean and Climate Variables.
introduction.paragraph3: These observations flow into data systems and are crucial for tracking, predicting and adapting to climate change, accurate weather and extreme event prediction, monitoring biodiversity for achieving key global targets, and informing sound decisions by local communities and national governments around sustainable development.
